full_judgment:
8. Learned appellate Judge in recording reversal rendered decision that the plaintiff-appellant stated that amicably Hasen got the suit-land whose heirs were Neoti Bibi, Rabeya and Jahuruddin from whom he purchased the suit land by three registered deeds dated 30.11.1981 Exhibit-1 series followed by a Bainapatra dated 15.2.1967 but the said Bainapatra has not been produce before this court. Learned appellate judge found contradictions in the testimonies of P.W.1, 2 and P.W.4 on the execution of Bainapatra and the passing of Baina money of Taka 9,800/- and took the view that simple contradictions of the testimony of P.W.4 was not sufficient to turn down plaintiff's claim in as much as P.Ws.1, 2 and 4 stated that rest amount of Taka 7,200/- was paid at the time of registration of deeds. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of evidences and facts held that vendors of plaintiff were heirs of Hasen Ali and the deeds, Exhibit-1 series of the plaintiff were genuine and the plaintiff got title to the suit land. Learned appellate Judge took into account the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 217 enunciating proposition that Rent Receipts though not documents of title, are important piece of evidence and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title and found that said ruling would be relevant if the defendant-respondent could have produced Dhakilas of the Ex-land-lord in the name of Banuram Muchi and held that the learned Munsif misconceived the law. Learned appellate Judge found that in the absence of any document showing that plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant it could not be considered at all that the plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant. Learned appellate Judge also took the view that Record of Right is simply a presumption of possession and the plaintiff having being in possession of the suit property, he was entitled to get the decree. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of the evidences of D.W.2 disbelieved the story of dispossession set up by the defendant. Learned appellate Judge totally ignored the story of waqf and found that the same was an insurance of the suit land in the premium of religion. 

 24. Defendant paid rents to Government Acquired Estate and got three Rent Receipts Exhibit-Cha series and Exhibit-Cha series are evidence of possession. This evidence of possession had been strengthened by State Acquisition Record of Right standing in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi the father of defendant. Ekhibit Ga Counterfoil of Twelve (12) Rent Receipts to monthly tenants Exhibit chha series. Municipal Tax Payment Receipts Exhibit-Jha series. Tahsilder letter to defendant's father Abdul Khaleque Munshi demanding payment of rent Exhibit-Yon. E.P.A.D.C. letter dated 30.7.1966, to E.P.A.D.C. forwarding a letter of cheque for payment of monthly rent Exhibit Ta Plaintiff could not produce a single Rent Receipt evidence payment of rent to Government Acquired Estate, any Municipal Tax Receipt 'manifesting payment of rent to Municipality. This non-payment of Rent raises a legal presumption that they had never been the owner and possessor of the suit property. Trial court on discussion and consideration of evidences recorded positive decision that plaintiff was a trespasser on the suit property and this positive decision rendered by trial court was not reversed by court of appeal. 

 31. True it is that defendant failed to lead evidence in support of acquisatien of title by Banuram Muchi but from series of documentary evidences. Exhibit-Ga. State Acquisition. Record of Right standing in the name of the defendant, Eihibit-Cha series, Rent Receipts. Exhibit-Chha series, Counterfoil of Twelve (12) Rent Receipts to monthly tenants and other Exhibits such as Yon and Ta Title and possession of defendant over the suit property was proved. The presumption attached to the State Acquisition Record of Right under section 144A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act could not be rebutted by plaintiff though rebuttable evidences. In the event of conflict between old Record of Right and recent Record of Right, recent Record of Right would prevail in asmuch as presumption of Record of Right looses its weight with the passage of time and entry in the subsequent Khatian would be mere acceptable than the entry in the earlier Khatian. Support for this proposition of law is sought to be drawn from Abdul Humid and others Vs. Abul Hossain Mir being dead his heirs Abdus Sobhan Mir and others 35 DLR (HCD)295.
